title: Apply for a conveyancer licence – individual
summary: You can apply for a conveyancer licence online to conduct legal work related to property transactions.
intro:
A conveyancer licence allows you to do legal work in relation to property transactions such as a sale or lease of land, or the granting of a mortgage. You can apply for a licence online.

You must have a conveyancer licence to conduct a conveyancing business for fee or reward unless you are:
who_can_apply: Be a fit and proper person to hold a licence.
Meet the criteria regarding qualifications and experience.
Not be a 'disqualified person' under the Conveyancers Licensing Act 2003.
Have paid the relevant contribution to the Property Services Compensation Fund.
what_you_need: Copies of your qualifications in PDF or JPG format.
Details of your previous conveyancing work experience.
The name and contact details of a referee regarding your work experience (you must seek their consent first).
Completed copies of applicable forms (in PDF or JPG format):
A copy of your Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) business name certificate (if trading under a business name).

how_to_steps.text: Follow the prompts to apply for a conveyancer licence.
Download and complete the Application for an individual conveyancer licence – PDF.
Gather the required supporting documents as indicated on the form.
Submit your application at a Service NSW Centre.

faqs.q: What does a conveyancer licence allow me to do?
faqs.a: A conveyancer licence allows you to do legal work related to property transactions, such as a sale or lease of land, or the granting of a mortgage.

faqs.q: Who must have a conveyancer licence?
faqs.a: You must have a conveyancer licence to conduct a conveyancing business for fee or reward.

You must be aged 18 or over, be a fit and proper person, meet qualification and experience criteria, and not be a 'disqualified person' under the Conveyancers Licensing Act 2003. You must also meet mandatory insurance requirements and have paid the relevant contribution to the Property Services Compensation Fund.
